title: Attestation lifecycle: slimline proofs & delegated approval PRD (concept draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD sketch for a lightweight attestation lifecycle for customer-managed networking changes and operator actions in Private deployments. Goal is to provide small, verifiable proof artifacts that Redwood and the customer can exchange/retain to satisfy audits without shipping large telemetry blobs across the WAN, and to define UX/approval primitives for delegated operators and customer admins.

Why now:
- Customers asking for minimal proof payloads for regulatory audits (finance/healthcare)
- Current design (full trace + telemetry) is heavy for low-bandwidth or air-gapped installs
- We need a pragmatic path to support delegated approvals and time-bound operator access with cryptographic receipts.

High-level goals:
- Define a compact attestation object ("proof capsule") containing: action-id, actor, timestamp, intent-hash, signature, short evidence pointers (hashes or local snapshot ids).
- Approval gate primitives: allow customer admins to pre-authorize operator change templates, require step-up for high-risk actions, and emit proof capsules for each approval decision.
- Design UX for canary/rollback: attach proof capsules to rollout events so canary rollback decisions are auditable.
- Minimize cross-network data: proofs are small (<= 2KB) and include hashes that reference richer local evidence (stored by customer or in optional encrypted blobs).

Non-goals:
- Not a full SIEM export design (we continue to support full telemetry options separately).
- Not solving long-term forensics storage policy (we provide hooks and export APIs but not retention engine in this PRD).

Principles:
- Small immutable token: proofs should be tiny, signed, and verifyable offline.
- Chainability: proofs can reference parent proofs (e.g., operator approval -> change execution -> rollback).
- Least privilege UX: make it easy to pre-approve safe templates, but require elevated flow for escalations.
- Customer-first data placement: allow proof verification without requiring Redwood to hold full evidence.

Proof capsule (proto sketch, human readable):
- version: v1
- id: UUID
- action: string (e.g., "vpc-change.apply-rule")
- actor: "user:alice@cust.com" | "operator:redwood-ops/engine-42"
- actor_role: short enum (admin|operator|service)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- intent_hash: SHA256(hex) of the canonical intent blob (compact JSON of params)
- evidence_refs: list of small pointers (e.g., local-snapshot:sha256, s3://bucket/path@sha256) limited to 3 items
- approval_policy_id: optional short id linking to the policy that authorized the action
- signature: base64(sig) by the signing key (customer or Redwood depending on flow)
- outcome: enum (approved|denied|executed|rolled_back)
- parent_proof_id: optional UUID
- notes: optional free text (<= 140 chars)

Notes on evidence_refs: they MUST be verifiable by providing the referenced blob + original intent. We anticipate customers will hold the heavy evidence; Redwood will store the capsule and optionally an encrypted evidence blob if configured.

Approval flows (sketch):
1) Template-based pre-approval (low friction): customer creates change templates (IP ranges, port rules, egress caps). Templates are tagged safe-by-default and pre-authorized for operators in a role. Each execution emits a proof capsule referencing the template id and an intent_hash.
2) Step-up approval (high risk): template not eligible or parameters exceed threshold -> request sent to admin for OOB approval (email/slack/console). Admin approves -> signed proof capsule returned.
3) Delegated escalation: customer can delegate approval rights to a 3rd-party operator for a limited window. Delegation itself emits a proof capsule (delegation record) chaining to subsequent approvals.

Risk model and mitigations:
- Replay: include nonces/timestamps and parent_proof chaining; require strict clock skew checks in verification.
- Tamper: signatures guard capsules; evidence stored off-chain can be validated by matching hashes.
- Loss of local evidence: recommend customer retention policy and optional encrypted snapshot export to Redwood (opt-in) for SRE-assisted forensics.

Integration with Private deployment networking model:
- Hook points: operator CLI/API -> control-plane agent -> local operator (edge) that can sign capsules with customer key (if customer-keyed) or Redwood key (if delegated).
- Air-gapped installs: proofs can be exported via USB or internal ticketing systems; verification tooling must accept offline verification by uploading capsules and verifying signatures + referenced evidence blobs.

Observability & Console UX (initial ideas):
- Proof timeline per change: show capsule chain (delegation -> approval -> execution -> rollback). Each item exposes the minimal capsule and links to evidence if available.
- Compact search: allow search by intent_hash, actor, template_id, or approval_policy_id.
- Alerts: policy violations (e.g., operator executed non-template action) trigger "audit exceptions" with links to the capsule and suggested rollback commands.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Define capsule v1 JSON schema and sign/verify reference implementation (sdk + CLI).
- Implement template-based pre-approval flow in control-plane and emit capsules on action execution.
- Console: basic proof timeline view for a single change with capsule JSON and link to evidence (if present).
- Offline verification: provide CLI that verifies capsule signature and resolves evidence_refs when local blobs are supplied.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Key management: prefer customer KMS for signatures — define KMS integration UX and fallback options. (ACTION: Priya to propose KMS UX)
- What is the canonical canonicalization for intent JSON? Must be stable across versions. (ACTION: Diego to draft canonicalizer)
- Retention default: how long do we retain capsules in Redwood hosted control plane? 90 days? 1 year? Need legal input. (link to legal thread)
- Delegation revocation: immediate revoke semantics vs grace period — how to handle in-flight operations?

Runbook excerpt (operator-facing):
- If a capsule verification fails: check clock skew, fetch parent_proof, request re-provision of evidence from customer archive.
- If an operator performs an unauthorized change: emit an incident with capsule and mark state for rollback.

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Q4 2025: prototype capsule schema + CLI + control-plane emitters
- Q1 2026: console timeline + basic search + KMS integration proof-of-concept
- Q2 2026: delegated approval primitives + policy engine hooks

References & links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-9872 (attestation strategy brief)
- Jira: JIRA-PLT-3241 (proof capsule RFC)
- Proto PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proof-proto/pull/48

Appendix: very compact example capsule (v1, pretty JSON):
{
  "version": "v1",
  "id": "b3f2d7e6-7a1c-4a9d-9b8f-f1e3a2c5d2b7",
  "action": "vpc-change.apply-rule",
  "actor": "user:alice@cust.com",
  "actor_role": "admin",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-03-08T14:32:10Z",
  "intent_hash": "3a7f1e...afc9",
  "evidence_refs": ["local-snapshot:sha256:ab12..."],
  "approval_policy_id": "tpl-42",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ...",
  "outcome": "executed",
  "parent_proof_id": null,
  "notes": "applied via template-safety"
}

-- end draft --

(If useful, I can split this into separate RFC + UX sketch docs. Want feedback from SRE/security and legal on retention & KMS.)
